title: What Prevents Me?
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: The eunuch had just been turned away from the temple. Nothing about his condition changed. The only difference was Christ.
exhortation: I wanted to come back to Acts 8, which our pastor preached on this week. I was very impacted by the story of Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch. So many wondrous things happen in it, but I want to pick it up where Philip finds out what passage the eunuch is reading: Isaiah 53, "Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter." Philip opens his mouth and, beginning with that Scripture, tells him the good news about Jesus. Then they come to some water, and the eunuch says, "See, here is water! What prevents me from being baptized?"

That question is what struck me. Probably only weeks or days before, the eunuch had been at the temple. He had traveled for months through deserts and seas, likely because of the rumor of God's presence there. He longed to experience it and to have that access. But as a eunuch, he couldn't enter. Someone in his condition was specifically prohibited. He didn't measure up, he wasn't worthy, and there was nothing he could fix or do to get in.

So as Philip unfolds the mystery of Jesus, the Lamb led to the slaughter, I can almost hear the hesitation in the eunuch's voice. I don't think his question was rhetorical at all. He had just been rejected at the temple. He must have thought, "There has to be a catch. It sounds too good. What will keep me out this time?"

But nothing about the eunuch's condition had changed. Did he measure up now? No. Was he somehow worthy now? No. Had he learned some secret rule that would finally get him in? No. The only difference was Christ. He needed the good news about Jesus, and Philip gave it to him: that Jesus measured up in his place.
prayer: Lord, thank you. We recognize that we are not worthy. In ourselves we can't come before you clean, pure and righteous. There is impurity and unrighteousness in us, and we know it. And yet you welcome us, not because you brushed justice aside or decided sin was okay, but because you paid for our unrighteousness. You bled and died. You received the shame we deserved, so that we might be cleansed and made righteous, and come before you with joy, thanksgiving and gratitude for what you have done. Thank you, Jesus.

We pray for anyone who feels their unrighteousness and unworthiness and knows it to be true. Help them humble themselves under your grace and love and receive the cleansing and forgiveness found in Jesus. In your precious name, Jesus. Amen.
